_readme: Data for tools/win_port.py. The Windows edition is a regeneration of the
Linux one, not a fork: every feature comes from ~/browser, and only the
regions described here are ours. Keep this file honest and the port stays
a script run plus a diff review.
'ported_from' is the Linux commit the checked-in Windows files were last
generated from. win_port.py uses it as the merge base, so it MUST be
updated (the script does it) whenever a port is committed.
'linux_repo' is where that checkout is. This file is committed and
public, so it says ~ rather than naming a home directory; win_port.py
expands it. An absolute path works too.

_edited_here_readme: Ported files this edition then changes, and why. Each one is a merge_file
rather than a copy_file, so the change survives the next port and a Linux
edit to the same lines raises a conflict instead of being silently lost.
Anything here is a divergence and wants a reason that will still read as a

edited_here.test_upgrade.py: checks an old browser.py out of THIS repository; the revision the Linux copy names is a Linux commit, and the two histories share nothing
edited_here.README.md: the same document for a different machine: the install is a zip and a .bat, the paths are %LOCALAPPDATA%, the screenshots are Windows ones, the agent bridge and the security-check workflow belong to the Linux repository, and the tail of it explains this port instead of pointing at it. A merge_file so a feature list that grows there grows here too

_substitutions_readme: Applied to generated files after the merge/copy. Written so that running
them twice is a no-op: the replacement never matches the pattern again.
'min' is a floor on hits, and it is low on purpose. browser.py comes out
of the three-way merge with our side's substitutions already in it, so it
contributes nothing here; a rule only fires for it when Linux adds a NEW
font stack, which is exactly the case worth catching. The copied HTML
pages are fresh from Linux every time, so those hits are guaranteed.
What actually enforces the result is the matching marker below.
They are applied to the test files too, and on purpose: a suite that
asserts the browser's font stack is asserting something about the edition
it is run against, and in this one that stack really is the Windows one.
test_look2 pinned the terminal look's `monospace` fallback and failed here

A 'find' or 'replace', and a marker 'pattern', may be a LIST of fragments instead of a string; win_port.py joins them with nothing between. That is not decoration. The strings these rules exist to keep out are his home directory, the subnet his own machines sit on and his mail handle, and a rule that spelled one out would put it in this public repo -- which is the leak, and which gitguard's pre-commit refuses, correctly. Splitting the needle is how the guard names what it forbids without carrying it.

_hand_regions_readme: Regions that are NOT reproduced by merge+substitution and only survive
because the 3-way merge carries them forward from the previous port. They
are listed here so a reviewer knows what to look for, and so a from-scratch
regeneration (no merge base) knows what it must re-add by hand.
The markers above are what actually enforces their presence.
This was four regions and is now one. The other three (the data folder's
Windows default, the icacls helper and the branch in _write_private, the
taskbar identity and the .ico) live in ~/browser itself as of 2026-10-22,
where test_winbranch.py can reach them - the Linux file was already calling
_restrict_to_owner from _write_atomic without defining it, which is what a
divergence costs. What is left here is the updater, and it is here because
it genuinely cannot be shared: this edition is unzipped, not cloned, and it
updates itself from its own repository.
hand_regions: Bridge._update_without_clone (the zip body, not the Linux sentence) and Bridge._zip_update

_win_only_files_readme: Files that exist only in this edition and must never be clobbered by a port. CHANGELOG.md is here because each edition tells its own story: the Linux changelog names Linux commits and Linux-only work, and merging the two would read as neither. README.md is NOT here - it is a merge_file, see edited_here.
_linux_only_files_readme: Files in ~/browser that deliberately do not come across, and why.

linux_only_files.install.sh: POSIX installer; install.bat is this edition's equivalent
linux_only_files..github/: CI runs on the Linux repository
linux_only_files.engine_pane.py: the experimental pane renders through web_engine.so, built from ~/claude/web-engine on that machine; there is no Windows build, and browser.py already treats the module as optional
linux_only_files.mpris.py: MPRIS is a D-Bus protocol of the Linux desktop; Windows answers the media keys through SystemMediaTransportControls, which Qt does not expose
linux_only_files.agent.py: the scripting bridge listens on an AF_UNIX socket under /tmp; a Windows port wants a named pipe and is not written yet
linux_only_files.agent_bridge.py: the other half of that socket
linux_only_files.test_agent.py: tests agent.py, which does not come across
linux_only_files.test_agent2.py: tests agent.py, which does not come across
linux_only_files.test_agentops.py: tests agent.py, which does not come across
linux_only_files..gitignore: nearly the same file, but the Linux one ignores web_engine.so, the compiled artifact of the engine pane, which does not exist here
